A force always directed back to the equilibrium position.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Oscillations — a core area of A-Level Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Oscillations brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Oscillations.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

options: Damping is critical.
The driving frequency matches the natural frequency.
Amplitude is zero.
Energy is conserved.

mcqs.q: Heavy damping in a car suspension causes:
options: Continuous oscillation at high amplitude.
Slow return to equilibrium without oscillation.
Resonance.
Increased natural frequency.

mcqs.q: For a projectile launched horizontally, what affects the horizontal component of velocity during flight (ignoring air resistance)?
options: The horizontal velocity increases over time because the projectile is falling.
The wall pushes back with a force proportional to how stiff it is, not equal to your force.
Nothing — horizontal velocity stays constant; only vertical velocity changes due to gravity.
Gravity slows down both the vertical and horizontal motion.

mcqs.q: What distinguishes gamma rays from X-rays of the same frequency?
options: The horizontal velocity increases over time because the projectile is falling.
Origin — gamma rays come from nuclear processes; X-rays come from electron transitions or deceleration of charged particles.
Gamma rays are slower than X-rays.
Gamma rays have higher frequency than any X-ray.

mcqs.q: When you push a wall, what does Newton's third law say about the wall?
options: The wall exerts an equal and opposite force on you at the same instant.
The wall only pushes back if your force is strong enough to make it react.
Gamma rays are slower than X-rays.
The wall pushes back with a force proportional to how stiff it is, not equal to your force.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Critical damping”?
options: The minimum damping that returns the system to equilibrium without oscillation in the shortest time.
Reduction of amplitude of oscillations due to dissipation of energy as heat.
Large-amplitude oscillation when the driving frequency equals the natural frequency.
Oscillation of a system at its natural frequency with no external driving force.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Damping”?
options: Reduction of amplitude of oscillations due to dissipation of energy as heat.
Large-amplitude oscillation when the driving frequency equals the natural frequency.
Oscillation produced by a periodic external driving force.
The minimum damping that returns the system to equilibrium without oscillation in the shortest time.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Natural frequency”?
options: Reduction of amplitude of oscillations due to dissipation of energy as heat.
The frequency at which a system oscillates when displaced and released without external driving.
The minimum damping that returns the system to equilibrium without oscillation in the shortest time.
Oscillation of a system at its natural frequency with no external driving force.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Free oscillation”?
options: Oscillation produced by a periodic external driving force.
Oscillation of a system at its natural frequency with no external driving force.
Large-amplitude oscillation when the driving frequency equals the natural frequency.
The minimum damping that returns the system to equilibrium without oscillation in the shortest time.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Forced oscillation”?
options: Oscillation produced by a periodic external driving force.
The minimum damping that returns the system to equilibrium without oscillation in the shortest time.
Oscillation of a system at its natural frequency with no external driving force.
The frequency at which a system oscillates when displaced and released without external driving.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Resonance”?
options: Reduction of amplitude of oscillations due to dissipation of energy as heat.
Large-amplitude oscillation when the driving frequency equals the natural frequency.
The minimum damping that returns the system to equilibrium without oscillation in the shortest time.
Oscillation produced by a periodic external driving force.
